qt: to the Commission Nikola Bartůšek (ECR), Jacek Ozdoba (ECR), Kateřina Konečná (PfE), Nora Junco García (ECR), Marion Maréchal (ECR), Kosma Złotowski (ECR), Kristoffer Storm (ECR), Ondřej Knotek (PfE), Malika Sorel (NI), Katarína Roth Neveďalová (NI), Sebastian Tynkkynen (ECR), Ondřej Krutílek (ECR), Alexandr Vondra (ECR), Fernand Kartheiser (NI), Antonín Staněk (PfE), Georgiana Teodorescu (ECR), Alvise Pérez (NI), Jessika van Leeuwen (ECR) Subject:

On 13 November 2026, ministers from nine Member States – Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, Finland, Greece, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Poland – reportedly asked Commissioner Brunner in a joint letter to revise Council Directive 2003/86/EC1 so that Member States may lawfully restrict family reunification. In its answer to Written Question E-003123/20252 of 26 September 2025, the Commission stated that it was not planning to revise the directive and was focusing on monitoring its implementation, including through a European Migration Network study. At an exchange of views with the European Conservatives and Reformists Group on 6 October 2026, Commissioner Brunner indicated that this approach is being reconsidered. However, the Commission work programme 2027, adopted on 4 November 2026, contains no initiative on family reunification. 1.
Does the Commission intend to propose a revision of Council Directive 2003/86/EC, and if so, by when?
How will it follow up on the request of the nine Member States and will it involve Parliament, as co-legislator, from the outset?
When will it publish the results of its monitoring of the directive’s implementation, including the European Migration Network study?
